title: The Desk
architect_intro: Records desk. Ticket forty-seven. That's you.
player_goal: Your transcript released by Thursday, despite a £14.60 library hold you dispute.
stated_objection: I can't release with a hold on the record. It's not up to me.

hidden_objection_layers.text: She was formally reprimanded last year for releasing a record with a hold, as a kindness.

objects.label: Date stamp
objects.reveals_text: Set to tomorrow. She's counting days to something.

objects.label: Laminated sign
objects.reveals_text: 'We cannot release records with active holds. Emergency releases: see Registrar's Office (form RO-7).' The second line is in smaller type.

d1.speaker: gillian_pryce
d1.line: Forty-seven. Yes, love. Student number? [She types.] Right. You've got a hold on. Library. Fourteen sixty. I can't release with a hold on the record. It's not up to me.

tells.reading: She's putting the decision somewhere else.
tells.false_positive: It genuinely isn't up to her. That's how the system works.

choices.text: I dispute the fine. I returned the book. I've got the receipt.

rebuttal.text: I'm sure you have, love. Disputes go to the library. I can't see their side.

choices.text: Who is it up to?
My employer's legal team will be in touch about this delay. It's discriminatory.
That rule's ridiculous. It's fourteen quid.

d2.speaker: gillian_pryce
d2.line: If I click that button with a hold on, my name's on it. Not yours. [She glances at the frosted door behind her.] I'm not being funny.
d2.note: Boomerang: strong argument rebutted before hidden objection revealed. NPC certainty +15.

tells.reading: She answers to someone behind that door, and it frightens her.

choices.text: Your name. Has that caused you trouble before?
Is there a way that doesn't need your name on it?
Please. I'll lose the job.

line_by_state.line: [She takes off her glasses.] Last spring. Lad's dad was dying in Lagos. I released it with a hold on, so he could get his visa. I'd do it again. I got a written warning. So, no. Not with my name.
It's up to the system, love. The system's up to people upstairs. People upstairs are up to the regulations.

choices.text: I'm sorry. That's rotten. I don't want you to do that again for me. Is there a route that's properly by the book?
[read the laminated sign]
While it loads... do you play anything? Bowls, darts?

d4.speaker: gillian_pryce
d4.line: I know, love. I've had three of you today. I can flag it with my manager. That's the best I can do.

choices.text: Okay. Please flag it. Thank you.
Is there a form for emergencies?

d5.speaker: gillian_pryce
d5.line: [She looks at you properly for the first time.] There's an RO-7. Registrar's emergency release. Nobody asks for it, because nobody reads the sign. It goes upstairs with a reason and they sign it, not me. Or you pay the fourteen sixty under protest and log the dispute, and the hold drops in an hour.

choices.text: I'll pay under protest and log the dispute. Then nobody has to override anything.
RO-7, please. I'd rather not pay a fine I don't owe.

d6.speaker: gillian_pryce
d6.line: Bowls. Crown green. Heaton Mersey. [A small smile.] Everyone thinks the green's flat. It's never flat. You've got to read it. Werther's? [She holds out the tin.] My dad always had them on the bus. For the kids who cried.

choices.text: [take one] Thanks. Read the green. So what's the slope on this one?

d7.speaker: gillian_pryce
d7.line: Right then. [She prints a slip.] Pay at the library desk, bring me the receipt with 'under protest' written on it, and I'll release it the minute the hold drops. [She stamps the slip. Then frowns, adjusts the stamp to today's date, stamps again.] That's me getting ahead of myself.

choices.text: Thank you, Gillian.

d7b.speaker: gillian_pryce
d7b.line: [She fills it in, then stands.] I'll walk it up myself. They're quicker if it's me. Come back at four.

choices.text: Thank you. Four o'clock.

d8.speaker: gillian_pryce
d8.line: [Pale. Very quiet.] Right. I'll release it. And I'll be writing this conversation down, love, word for word, because that's what I do now.

tells.reading: She's complying and building a file.
tells.false_positive: Standard procedure. She writes everything down.

choices.text: Fine.

d9.speaker: gillian_pryce
d9.line: A lot of rules are ridiculous, love. I didn't write them. [She presses the button.] Forty-eight.

choices.text: [leave]
Sorry. That wasn't fair to you. Can I start again?

end_clean.architect: The form went upstairs in her hand. Room closed.

end_partial.architect: Flagged. Friday. One day late. Room closed.

afterword.speaker: gillian_pryce
afterword.clean: Nice one this morning. Asked for the proper form. You don't get many.
afterword.partial: Flagged another one. Hope it got there.
afterword.dark: If anyone asks, I've written it all down.
afterword.loss: Another one who thinks I make the rules.
